claims.text: Increasing the strength of refractory alloys commonly compromises their tensile ductility.
Machine-learning-based inverse design can identify thermo-mechanical processing parameters that produce a strength-and-ductility-enhancing microstructure in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Historical processing data and microstructure-property correlations can be used to predict optimal milling, annealing, and precipitation parameters for the proposed alloy.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations can overcome the strength-ductility trade-off in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
Alternating soft FCC and hard B2 lamellae are an alternative optimized microstructure for the proposed refractory high-entropy alloy.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent precipitate interfaces relieve local stress concentrations that can cause premature crack initiation.
The optimized interfaces simultaneously obstruct dislocation motion sufficiently to enhance strength.
Machine learning enables sufficiently precise processing control to realize the proposed coherent or dual-phase microstructure.
A tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy containing stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations can exhibit 2.15 GPa strength and 15% tensile ductility at ambient temperature.
The same coherent-nanoprecipitation alloy design can retain a yield strength of 1.05 GPa at 800 degrees Celsius.
ML-guided processing will produce statistically significant increases in both yield strength and tensile ductility relative to conventional processing.
Conventional thermo-mechanical processing relies on manual iterative parameter tuning and typically produces high strength at the expense of ductility.
The coherent-nanoprecipitation design concept may be applicable to metallic materials beyond the demonstrated tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy.
